mainTopic: Produce returned to the תחום (רבי נחמיה's 'במקומן'), and walking and carrying in a valley walled in on שבת
overview: The amud opens by asking what רבי נחמיה means when he says produce 'במקומן' (in its place) may be eaten. That cannot mean produce returned on purpose, because another ברייתא has רבי נחמיה permit only an accidental return. So the גמרא fills in missing words (חסורי מחסרא): the תנא קמא permits produce back in its place even if it was returned במזיד, and רבי נחמיה permits it only if it was returned בשוגג. The גמרא tries another reading, in which everyone forbids a deliberate return. It rejects that reading because the wording of the סיפא shows the תנא קמא permits even a deliberate return. Then רב נחמן brings two rulings in the name of שמואל. First, someone who does not know his תחום may count 2,000 medium steps. Second, someone in a valley that נכרים walled in on שבת may walk 2,000 אמה but may carry in the whole enclosure by throwing. רב הונא disagrees: carry only ד' אמות. The גמרא explains his reasons: the person might follow his object, and his zone is like a wall breached completely toward a forbidden area. A statement of חייא בר רב is reread as support for רב הונא. Finally, רב נחמן tells רב הונא that a ברייתא supports שמואל, and the ברייתא is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's ruling about produce in its place
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says that produce 'in its place' may be eaten, and produce 'not in its place' may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: If the produce is in its place, it may be eaten. If it is not in its place, it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of a ברייתא, which is רבי נחמיה's added opinion about produce that went outside the תחום שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא made the rule depend on whether the produce left בשוגג or במזיד. רבי נחמיה instead uses the word 'במקומן,' meaning whether the produce is back in its original place. He does not say how it got back, and that gap is what the גמרא will now ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place, meaning the produce was brought back to its original location.
The boundary on שבת, 2000 אמות beyond the town, past which one may not walk or carry.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
If in their place, they may be eaten;
phrases.notes: The produce was returned inside the תחום.

phrases.english: if not in their place, they may not be eaten.
phrases.notes: The produce is still outside the תחום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא begun on the previous amud (41b).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce returned to its place may be eaten. Produce still outside its place may not.

steps.title: What does 'in its place' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of return רבי נחמיה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'in its place' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next step: what exactly does רבי נחמיה mean by 'in its place'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce can get back to its place in two ways: by accident (שוגג) or on purpose (מזיד). The question is which of these רבי נחמיה means.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'in their place'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'במקומן' mean the produce was returned on purpose or by accident?

steps.title: It cannot mean returned on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'in its place' means 'returned on purpose,' then rejects this because another ברייתא has רבי נחמיה require an accidental return.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'in its place' means it was returned on purpose, that is difficult. Another ברייתא clearly teaches: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say the produce is always forbidden unless it was returned to its place by accident. So an accidental return helps, but an intentional return does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning, 'returned on purpose,' and immediately knocks it down with a contradicting source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי נחמיה permitted produce returned במזיד. That would contradict his own clear statement elsewhere, where only a return בשוגג makes the produce permitted. So 'במקומן' cannot mean an intentional return.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected).

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אִילֵּימָא' as the גמרא's conclusion. It is only a suggestion, and the גמרא is about to reject it.

phrases.english: If you say: 'in their place' means returned intentionally,
but it is explicitly taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov say:
They are always forbidden,
phrases.notes: One may carry them no more than four אמות.

phrases.english: unless they return to their place unintentionally.
So: unintentionally, yes; intentionally, no.
phrases.notes: This is what the גמרא learns from that ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא: בִּמְקוֹמָן — בְּמֵזִיד, וְהָא קָתָנֵי בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one answer to the question in step 2 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'במקומן' means an intentional return.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא records רבי נחמיה permitting only an unintentional return. He cannot also permit an intentional one.

steps.title: It means returned by accident, and the ברייתא is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'in its place' means returned by accident. It explains that the ברייתא is missing words and begins to fill them in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'in its place' must mean it was returned by accident. The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it means: Produce that went out beyond the תחום, if it went out by accident, may be eaten. If it went out on purpose, it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: With 'אֶלָּא לָאו' ('Rather, is it not...?'), the גמרא proposes that 'in its place' means 'returned by accident.' It then starts rebuilding the full ברייתא, since some words are missing from the text as we have it. Step 7 will test this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As written, the ברייתא does not show what רבי נחמיה is arguing against. The גמרא says words are missing (חסורי מחסרא). It begins by restating the first opinion: going out בשוגג permits eating, and going out במזיד forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (introduces the correct reading)
And this is what it teaches.

steps.confusionAlert: 'חסורי מחסרא' does not mean the ברייתא is wrong. It means some words are left out, and the גמרא fills them in to show what the ברייתא really means.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean: 'in their place' means returned unintentionally,
and the text is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Produce that went out beyond the תחום:
if unintentionally, it may be eaten; if intentionally, it may not be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו: בִּמְקוֹמָן — בְּשׁוֹגֵג, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after step 3 rejected the first suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'במקומן' means returned by accident. The ברייתא must be rebuilt with missing words.

steps.title: The missing words: back in place, even on purpose is fine
steps.stepSummary: The rebuilt ברייתא adds that the first opinion's rule applies only to produce still outside. Produce returned to its place may be eaten even if it was returned on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? When the produce is not in its place. But if it is back in its place, it may be eaten even if it was returned on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps filling in the missing words of the ברייתא. This part shows what the first opinion holds, which is what רבי נחמיה will argue against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion's line between שוגג and מזיד applies only while the produce is still outside the תחום. Once the produce is back in its place, the first opinion permits it no matter how it got back, even במזיד. This sets up the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (limits a rule to a specific case)

phrases.english: In what case are these words said? When it is not in its place;
but if it is in its place, even if returned intentionally, it may be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues rebuilding the ברייתא started in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to the first opinion, produce returned to its place is permitted even if the return was intentional.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: even in its place, only an accidental return helps
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה argues that even after the produce is back in its place, only an accidental return permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נחמיה came to say: even when it is back in its place, the difference still applies. If it was returned by accident, yes, it is permitted. If it was returned on purpose, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by explaining what רבי נחמיה adds, which fits his statement in the other ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion permits produce once it is back in its place, however it got there. רבי נחמיה disagrees: even then, an intentional return does not make it permitted. This keeps רבי נחמיה consistent with the other ברייתא. Step 7 challenges this reading, and step 9 confirms it.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says produce back in its place is permitted even if returned במזיד. רבי נחמיה says even back in its place, only a return בשוגג permits it. This matches his view in the other ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא settles a sage's views across two ברייתות. It fills in missing words so that רבי נחמיה stays consistent.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya came to say:
even when it is in its place, too,
if unintentionally, yes; if intentionally, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rebuilt ברייתא by giving רבי נחמיה's disagreement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי נחמיה holds that produce back in its place is permitted only if it was returned by accident. This is consistent with the other ברייתא.

steps.title: Another way to read the argument: both sides forbid a deliberate return
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the תנא קמא permits a deliberate return. It suggests that everyone forbids a deliberate return to its place, and the argument is only about produce taken out by accident that is still outside the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If it was returned to its place on purpose, everyone agrees it is forbidden. Here they argue about produce taken out by accident that is not back in its place. The תנא קמא holds that if it was taken out by accident, it is permitted even when not in its place. רבי נחמיה holds that even when taken out by accident, it is permitted only if it is back in its place, and not if it is still outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No.' It refuses to accept that the תנא קמא permits produce returned on purpose, and it offers a different way to understand what the two sides argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this new reading, nobody permits a deliberate return. The argument moves to a different case: produce taken out בשוגג that is still outside. The תנא קמא permits it there. רבי נחמיה requires it to be back in its place first.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place, back inside the original תחום
Not in their place, still outside the תחום
Everyone agrees; there is no argument
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggested reading, and the very next step will reject it. Do not walk away thinking this is the final explanation of the argument.

phrases.english: No. If it was returned on purpose to its place,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back on the earlier idea that the תנא קמא allows bringing it back on purpose.

phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
Here they argue about produce taken out by accident that is not in its place.
phrases.notes: The argument is moved to a different case.

phrases.english: The first תנא holds
that if it was taken out by accident, it is permitted even when not in its place.
And רבי נחמיה holds that even when taken out by accident,
if it is back in its place, yes, it is permitted;
if it is not in its place, no, it is not permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּמֵזִיד בִּמְקוֹמָן — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from the rebuilt ברייתא and offers a different case as the subject of the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that the תנא קמא permits produce returned to its place on purpose.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read so that both sides forbid a deliberate return, with the argument only about accidental removal and no return.

steps.title: The wording of the סיפא shows the תנא קמא permits even a deliberate return
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the new reading. In the סיפא, רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב require the produce to be returned 'accidentally.' That implies the תנא קמא permits even a deliberate return.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the סיפא teaches that רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say the produce stays forbidden until it returns to its place by accident. So an accidental return works and a deliberate one does not. This implies the תנא קמא holds that even a deliberate return is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the reading from the last step. It points to the exact words רבי נחמיה uses in the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה stresses that the return must be שוגג. That only makes sense if someone else, the תנא קמא, permits a return done במזיד. So the argument must be about a deliberate return to its place, which is the opposite of what Step 7 suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
By implication; we learn it from what was said
A תנא who agrees with רבי נחמיה here

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov say:
They always remain forbidden
until they are returned to their place by accident.
So by accident, yes; on purpose, no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא learns this from the word שוגגין, 'by accident.'

phrases.english: This implies that the first תנא holds
that even on purpose, it is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the alternative reading of Step 7 and restores the earlier inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 7 that everyone forbids a deliberate return to its place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה specifies that the return must be accidental. That only makes sense if the תנא קמא permits a deliberate return.

steps.title: Conclusion: the original inference stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof. The תנא קמא permits produce returned to its place even on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. The proof from the סיפא is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The alternative reading from Step 7 is dropped. The final understanding is this: the תנא קמא permits produce returned to its place even במזיד, and רבי נחמיה requires a שוגג return. Per Sefaria's note, this supports רב פפא's view discussed earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא permits produce returned to its place even if it was returned on purpose. רבי נחמיה permits it only if it was returned by accident.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof brought in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the תנא קמא, produce returned to its place is permitted even if it was returned deliberately.

steps.title: Measuring the תחום שבת with ordinary steps
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: someone walking who does not know where his תחום שבת ends may walk 2,000 medium-sized steps, and that is his תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If someone was walking and does not know where the תחום שבת ends, he walks 2,000 medium steps, and that is the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a practical rule from שמואל about how to measure the תחום when you have no exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תחום is 2,000 אמה. One medium step is roughly one אמה, so counting 2,000 ordinary steps is an acceptable way to measure it.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת boundary: the 2,000 אמה limit for walking from where one rests
Medium-sized steps, each about one אמה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: If one was walking and does not know where the Shabbos limit is,
he walks two thousand medium steps,
and this is the Shabbos limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about measuring the תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 2,000 medium steps count as the 2,000 אמה of the תחום שבת.

steps.title: A valley walled in on שבת: walk 2,000, carry everywhere by throwing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: someone who rested in a valley that נכרים surrounded with a wall on שבת may walk only 2,000 אמה. He may carry anywhere in the enclosure, but only by throwing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן also said in the name of שמואל: If someone rested for שבת in a valley, and נכרים built a wall around it on שבת, he may walk 2,000 אמה, and he may carry in all of it by throwing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second rule from רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, about a wall that went up only after שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His walking limit was fixed when שבת began, before the wall existed, so the new wall does not extend his walking past 2,000 אמה. But the wall does turn the area into an enclosed space for carrying. So he may move objects into the farther parts, but only by throwing them, since he himself may not walk there.
steps.confusionAlert: The wall changes the carrying rules but not the walking limit. Walking and carrying are two separate issues here.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman also said in the name of Shmuel:
If one rested for Shabbos in a valley,
and non-Jews surrounded it with a wall on Shabbos,
he may walk only two thousand amos,
and he may carry in all of it by throwing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same speakers on a related תחום topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall built on שבת does not extend the walking limit past 2,000 אמה. It does allow carrying throughout the enclosure, but only by throwing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the walking limit is set at the start of שבת, while the status of an area for carrying can change once walls go up.

steps.title: רב הונא: walk 2,000 אמה, carry only ד' אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא disagrees with שמואל. The person may walk 2,000 אמה, but he may carry only ד' אמות at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: He may walk 2,000 אמה, and he may carry only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, from רב הונא, about the same case of the valley walled in on שבת. He agrees about walking but is stricter about carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שמואל and רב הונא agree the person may walk only 2,000 אמה. The difference is carrying. שמואל allowed carrying in the whole enclosure by throwing, while רב הונא allows moving objects only ד' אמות, the way one does in a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who here argues with שמואל's ruling
Four cubits, the small distance one may carry in a non-private area

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
He may walk two thousand cubits,
and he may carry only four cubits.
phrases.notes: Like the rule of a כרמלית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter alternative ruling to שמואל's ruling in step 11 about the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a valley walled in on שבת, one may walk 2,000 אמה but carry only ד' אמות.

steps.title: Why not carry in the whole area by throwing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. The walls make the area a private domain, so why not allow carrying throughout it by throwing, as שמואל said?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him carry in the entire enclosed area by throwing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב הונא's strict rule. It asks why carrying by throwing in the whole walled area should not be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The walls should turn the whole enclosure into a רשות היחיד. The person's own walking is limited, but throwing an object does not move him. So it seems there is no reason to forbid carrying by throwing anywhere in the enclosure.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of it, meaning the entire enclosure

phrases.english: And let him carry in all of it
by means of throwing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's restriction of carrying to ד' אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The walls make the area private, and throwing does not move the person. So carrying by throwing in the whole enclosure should be allowed.

steps.title: He might follow his object out of his limit
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbade throwing in case he follows the object beyond his 2,000 אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will be drawn after his object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why throwing is not allowed. It is a safeguard (a גזירה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he throws something past his 2,000 אמה, he may walk after it to get it and leave his תחום. To prevent that, the חכמים did not allow carrying by throwing in the whole area.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps or lest, used to introduce a safeguard

phrases.english: Lest he be drawn after his object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Throwing should be allowed since the person himself does not move.
steps.terutzMaskana: Throwing is forbidden because he might walk after the object and leave his תחום.

steps.title: Then at least carry normally within 2,000 אמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Within his own 2,000 אמה there is no fear of leaving his limit, so why not carry normally there?
steps.simpleTranslation: Within the 2,000 אמה, at least, let him carry in the normal way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רב הונא. The worry from step 14 does not apply inside the zone where he may walk anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if throwing across the whole enclosure is forbidden, inside his 2,000 אמה he is allowed to walk. Following his object there causes no problem. So it seems he should be allowed to carry normally in that zone, not just ד' אמות.

phrases.english: Within two thousand cubits, at least,
let him carry in the usual manner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 14 but points out that it does not explain the restriction within 2,000 אמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's limit of ד' אמות even inside the 2,000 אמה zone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fear of following the object does not apply where he may walk anyway. So normal carrying there should be allowed.

steps.title: The 2,000-אמה zone is like a fully breached wall
steps.stepSummary: His 2,000 אמה zone has no wall separating it from the rest of the enclosure, where he is forbidden to go. It is like a wall breached completely toward a forbidden area, so even there he may carry only ד' אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is like a wall that was breached in its full width toward a place that is forbidden to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason for רב הונא's rule. It uses a law of walls, not the worry about following the object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His permitted zone of 2,000 אמה lies inside a bigger enclosure, and the rest of that enclosure is forbidden to him. There is no wall between his zone and the forbidden part, so his zone is open on its whole side to a forbidden place. A wall breached completely like that does not count as a wall, so the zone is not a private domain and he may carry only ד' אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: That was breached along its entire width
A place where carrying is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: walk 2,000 אמה, carry only ד' אמות. Throwing in the whole area is forbidden lest he follow his object. Normal carrying within the 2,000 אמה is forbidden because that zone is like a fully breached wall opening into a forbidden area.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the walls the נכרים built are breached. They are whole. The 'breach' is the unwalled side of the person's own 2,000 אמה zone, which opens into the part of the enclosure that is forbidden to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one area can count as private for one purpose and not another. It depends on whether the specific person's permitted zone is properly closed off from places forbidden to him.

phrases.english: Because it is like a partition
that was breached in its entirety
into a place that is forbidden to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 with a new reason based on the laws of breached walls.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal principle (laws of a breached wall)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Inside the 2,000 אמה there is no reason to forbid normal carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 2,000 אמה zone is fully open to a forbidden area, so it is not a proper private domain. He may carry only ד' אמות.

steps.title: חייא בר רב allows carrying throughout the 2,000 אמה
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב rules that the person may walk 2,000 אמה and may also carry throughout those 2,000 אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: He may walk 2,000 אמה, and he may carry within 2,000 אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion from חייא בר רב about the same case of the walled enclosure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed carrying throughout the whole enclosure by throwing. רב הונא allowed walking 2,000 אמה but carrying only ד' אמות at a time. חייא בר רב takes a middle position: carrying is allowed, but only inside his own 2,000 אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the son of רב

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
He may walk two thousand cubits,
and he may carry within two thousand cubits.
phrases.notes: This is the new part. Carrying is allowed throughout his 2,000 אמה, not only ד' אמות at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the dispute between שמואל (via רב נחמן) and רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may walk 2,000 אמה and may carry anywhere within those 2,000 אמה.

steps.title: This opinion matches neither side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view חייא בר רב follows, since it fits neither רב נחמן nor רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is not like רב נחמן and not like רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bothered that חייא בר רב's ruling does not match either of the two known opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן (citing שמואל) allows carrying in the entire enclosure by throwing. רב הונא allows only ד' אמות. Carrying normally within exactly 2,000 אמה is a third view, and the dispute seemed to leave no room for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like this one and not like that one

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא כְּרַב נַחְמָן וְלָא כְּרַב הוּנָא!
phrases.english: It is neither like Rav Nachman nor like Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַב נַחְמָן וְלָא כְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just cited in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's ruling that one may carry within 2,000 אמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two established views are 'the whole enclosure' and 'ד' אמות only'. A middle view of '2,000 אמה' seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Correct the wording to four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the text: he may carry only ד' אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: he may carry within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the wording of חייא בר רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'ארבע' in place of 'אלפים', the ruling becomes: walk 2,000 אמה, but carry only ד' אמות. This removes the strange third opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, a correction of the text

phrases.english: Say: he may carry within four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling allowed carrying within 2,000 אמה, which matched no one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling allows carrying only ד' אמות.

steps.title: Then it is just רב הונא's opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the corrected version simply repeats רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as רב הונא's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a new problem with the correction: now the statement says nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא already said 'walk 2,000, carry ד' אמות'. If חייא בר רב said the same thing, why is it recorded as a separate statement?

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the correction made in Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once corrected, the statement is identical to רב הונא's, so it adds nothing as a separate opinion.

steps.title: It is a supporting statement for רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the line as 'and so said רבי חייא בר רב', a support for רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'And similarly רבי חייא בר רב said.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents חייא בר רב not as a new opinion but as agreeing with רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is not a problem. It shows that another authority holds like רב הונא. Now the dispute is only between שמואל and רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said, introducing a supporting voice

steps.whatToRemember: In the end there are only two views: שמואל (via רב נחמן) allows carrying throughout the enclosure, but only by throwing, and רב הונא, joined by חייא בר רב, allows only ד' אמות.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב.
phrases.english: Say: 'And similarly Rabbi Chiyya bar Rav said.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by reframing the statement as support rather than a separate opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the statement's role (support, not a new view)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חייא בר רב's statement was a separate opinion that merely repeated רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is recorded as agreement: 'and so said חייא בר רב'.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells רב הונא not to argue with שמואל, because a ברייתא follows שמואל's view. The ברייתא is about to be quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: Do not argue with שמואל, because a ברייתא was taught like him. As it was taught:
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן sets up a proof for שמואל. This line introduces a ברייתא, which will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן is not giving a new reason. He says an earlier source (a ברייתא) already supports שמואל, so an אמורא like רב הונא should not disagree. The actual proof comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The אמורא whose view רב נחמן reported, allowing carrying throughout the enclosure

steps.confusionAlert: This step ends with 'דתניא:' and does not quote the ברייתא yet. The proof itself continues in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Huna:
Do not argue with Shmuel,
for a baraita was taught in accordance with him.
As it was taught:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא being quoted starts on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּיפְלוֹג עֲלֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main dispute between שמואל and רב הונא and brings a source supporting שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling, reported by רב נחמן, that one may walk only 2,000 אמה but may carry throughout the walled enclosure by throwing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (quoted on the next amud, 42b).
